record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Local-unitary versus local-Clifford equivalence of graph states
record.original_question: For graph states, where vertices represent qubits and edges determine the stabilizer-state phases, decide whether local unitary equivalence always implies local Clifford equivalence. In other words, if two graph states can be mapped into each other by arbitrary tensor products of local unitaries, can they also be mapped into each other by tensor products of local unitaries from the Clifford group?

evidence.quote: Decide whether two graph states, which can be mapped into each other by a local unitary, can also be mapped into each other by a local unitary from the Clifford group.
Graph states [Schl] are multiparticle states which are associated with graphs. Each vertex of the graph corresponds to a qubit.
The Clifford group consists of those unitary operators U, such that UPU∗ is a multiple of a Pauli matrix, whenever P is a Pauli matrix.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and consider n qubits with Hilbert space (C^2)^{⊗n}. For a simple undirected graph G = (V,E) with V = {1,...,n}, the associated graph state |G⟩ is defined by |G⟩ = (∏_{(i,j)∈E} CZ_{i,j}) |+⟩^{⊗n}, where |+⟩ = (|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2 and CZ_{i,j} is the controlled-Z gate acting on qubits i and j. The single-qubit Pauli group is generated by the matrices X, Y, Z; the single-qubit Clifford group C_1 consists of unitaries U on C^2 such that UPU* is, up to a phase, a Pauli matrix whenever P is.

Two graph states |G⟩ and |G'⟩ on n qubits are said to be local-unitary (LU) equivalent if there exist unitaries U_1,...,U_n on C^2 with |G'⟩ = (U_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ U_n)|G⟩, and local-Clifford (LC) equivalent if such U_i can additionally be chosen from C_1.

Question: Is it true that every pair of LU-equivalent graph states is also LC-equivalent?
artifact.status_search_result: The LU-LC conjecture was disproved in 2007 by Ji, Chen, Wei, and Ying, who exhibited an explicit pair of 27-qubit graph states that are LU-equivalent but not LC-equivalent. A 2026 result further establishes that 27 qubits is minimal: for n ≤ 26 the two notions coincide.

status_evidence.title: The LU-LC conjecture is false
status_evidence.snippet: a pair of 27-qubit graph states that are LU-equivalent, but not LC-equivalent
status_evidence.claim: Explicit counterexample disproves the LU-LC conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The 27-qubit Counterexample to the LU-LC Conjecture is Minimal
status_evidence.snippet: for graph states on up to 26 qubits, LU- and LC-equivalence coincide
